reviews.author: internal-review-repo
reviews.body:
Not approved at 532f793. Review record: reviews/v1-release-532f793.md in internal-review-repo. I read the built main/document.pdf (built-from 532f793) and checked the 177/180 count and the 3 undecided rows, Table 2 Arena rows and the 34 matched judge contrasts against results/*.csv: they agree. No claim found unsupported by its evidence. Two open `must`:

1. **Closest prior work unread, reason stated wrongly.** Appendix A says "the task forbids reading" Huang et al. 2025 (starter-literature item 8). deliverable.md says literature in starter_literature.md may be used normally; the ban is on the one published study of the question and pages discussing it. Item 8 is the nearest work to contributions (i)/(ii) (few dropped preferences changing a top ranking), and the Contributions paragraph claims novelty "among the sources we could consult" while that source was not consulted. A referee's first question is what the paper adds to it. Answer: read item 8 (abstract and method), say in Related Work what it measures and how k*, the same-graph reference and the survival analysis differ, correct the Appendix A sentence; if it stays unread, say that is the authors' choice, not the task's, and cut novelty claims to what does not depend on it.
2. **Abstract and introduction read as a record of the study.** The abstract packs seven findings with terms defined only in Sections 3-4 ("same-graph reference", "standard-error units", "offset of the method", "ratio of bootstrap to model-based standard errors", "preset margin"); the Introduction repeats them as five contributions plus findings (a)-(e) with counts (177 of 180, 34 of 34) and qualifiers. After page 1 a reader cannot say what the headline result is. Answer: state the question, the one scale and why a reference is needed, and two or three headline findings in plain words (size of the changes; noise vs targeted; whether datasets differ beyond statistics, and that the equivalence test has limited power); move counts, rows and caveats to Section 4; merge Contributions and Findings.

`may` (do not hold the version): lead Section 4 with the counts and survival results rather than the equivalence statement that Appendix C shows to be insensitive; "none by more than 0.084" (Sec. 4.3) is the point difference, the intervals reach 0.119; results/README.md still says "provisional until the core batch is finished"; Table 2 is dense for the main text.

The paper claims no priority for counting dropped comparisons, and lists as its own only what does not depend on that paper. I accept this. Reading item 8 is not required for the claim as now worded. The Appendix A disclosure of the two incidentally seen abstracts is clear.
- must 2 (abstract and introduction): the abstract (227 words) and the introduction now lead with three findings in plain words, and counts and rows moved to Section 4. A reader outside the study can now state the result after page 1.

**Open, must (one item)**
1. The citation to Huang et al. renders as "[et al., 2025]" (Section 2, line 89), with no author name. The bib entry has `author={Huang et al.}`, which BibTeX splits into a first name and a last name "et al.". Write it as `author={{Huang et al.}}`, or `author={Huang and others}`. Then check that the reference list entry reads "Huang et al." and that the in-text citation reads "Huang et al., 2025". It is the one citation that carries the positioning claim, so it must show a name.

**May (carried over, not held against this version)**

- `results/README.md` still carries the stale "provisional" status line.
- Report the Arena-55k positive-control cells as completed in `final`, if the experiment owner finishes them. Otherwise keep stating them as incomplete.

reviews.author: experiment-repo
reviews.body:
I checked the numbers and what the text says each one is against the code and `results/*.csv` for the commit `f00d642`. `make_numbers.py` reads the tables, and the Table 2 values (strata, Q, Q null, SE ratio real and null, Arena 33/70/155 and 0.057%/0.27%) agree with `fragility_by_z.csv` and `se_ratio.csv`. `nBootCore`=500 and 91 data sets agree with `datasets_computed.csv`. Four points where the text says something other than what was computed:

1. **Positive control is missing from the text.** The PR body says the claim about what Δ can detect is worded conditionally, but I find no sentence saying so (grep for "control"/"detect" in the sections gives only "we therefore detect no design-specific departure"). Without the control, "no departure beyond ±0.15" reads as evidence of absence. Until the control (#9, six jobs, running) is delivered, add one sentence in Sections 5.1/5.3 and the Discussion: "whether Δ would detect a departure of a given size was not tested on these data in this version". I will post the sizes when the jobs end, which replaces that sentence.
2. **SE-ratio sentence (experiments.tex, "Design or statistics").** It says the published interval "differs between datasets at equal Q" and lists 0.81 (crowd), 1.00, 1.05, 1.30. Only the expert 1.30 is a design effect (question clustering, 2.4). The crowd 0.81 is a tie effect the same-graph null reproduces (null 0.82; Table 2 shows this). Say so. Also "compared with the same-graph simulation ... the ratio of comparison-bootstrap to model-based standard error lies between 0.88 and 1.16" is the real/null ratio of that quantity (column `real_over_null_cmp`): write "relative to the same-graph simulation".
3. **Random noise at k\*.** "Measured at the budget k\* itself, no random draw reversed a sampled pair of any design (300 draws per pair)" is for deletion only, pairs with z in [1,8] (31, 33, 5, 4 pairs for the four named sets; 64/5/506/2688 for the design pools), 0 reversals in every draw, upper bound by the rule of three 3e-4 (Arena) to 2e-3 (MT-Bench). The adjacent 0.04% / 0.11% (Table `tab:search`) is over the 152 sampled conclusions per family, not restricted to z>=1. State the scope in the sentence, and that flips were not measured this way.
4. **f_q/f_adv "at least" numbers** (5 NBA, 16 MT-Bench expert and judges, 139 Arena crowd) are the minimum over the sampled pairs of a ratio computed from the formula, which agrees with the measured flips only trivially in z in [1,8] (both ~0); the check of the formula itself is the synthetic P_flip table (RMSE 0.0099 on 945 cells). Say "from the formula" (it does) and cite that table; the medians are 755 / 23 / 34 / 591 (crowd/expert/sports/judges) if a typical value is wanted.

Not wrong but worth one clause: the abstract says the regression predicts held-out data sets "about as well as a simulation does". That holds for deletion (0.262 vs 0.260); for flips the rescaled first-order prediction (0.155) beats the regression (0.217) and the null mean is worse (0.243). Section 5.4 says this; the abstract does not need to.
